title: Implicit group-mapping produces transient owner privileges during SSO org-linking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: multiple customers reported short-lived owner-level access being observed for service accounts and SSO users during organization linking and group sync events. The access spike lasted seconds-to-minutes and coincided with org/group mapping updates and a burst of SSO assertion deliveries. This issue is a high-severity security problem: privileged access was transiently available and not captured reliably in audit logs. The ticket aims to triage, reproduce, patch the precedence logic, harden audit emission, and ship a mitigation for production in the next release window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure SSO provider with nested groups: Company > Engineering > Infra. Map SSO groups to RBAC roles: Engineering -> writer, Infra -> owner.
2) Create user Alice in SSO and include her in Engineering only; ensure Infra membership will be added by an external identity change shortly after.
3) Trigger an identity change that adds Alice to Infra via the IdP (simulate group sync burst).
4) Simultaneously create a long-lived service token belonging to a different service account that has Organization-level bindings evaluated via cached group intersections.

5) Observe in product: for ~5-90 seconds Alice and the service token execute owner-level actions (org-level deletes, billing reads) before correct membership reconciliation completes; audit logs show either missing or delayed privilege-elevation events.
6) Repeat under high load (simulating 500 assertion events/min) to increase likelihood of missing audit entries.
root_cause: Race between group-mapping precedence resolution, cached role intersections, and asynchronous audit emission. When IdP group assertions arrive during an ongoing org-linking or membership reconciliation, the RBAC v2 evaluator temporarily applies an optimistic merged principal that includes newly-discovered nested group memberships before final reconciliation completes. At the same time, the async audit logger batches events and drops or delays certain ephemeral 'grant' events under high throughput, leaving no reliable audit trail for the transient elevation.
proposed_fix: 1) Change precedence: during SSO-driven membership changes, defer optimistic application of nested-group-derived admin/owner privileges until the reconciliation pass completes and canonical membership is written to the membership store. 2) Add a validation gate that treats owner-level grants produced by in-flight group syncs as provisional; block owner-scoped write operations until membership is fully persisted. 3) Make audit emission synchronous for critical privilege changes (owner/admin grants/revocations) or ensure guaranteed delivery for those events (durable queue with retries). 4) Add unit and integration tests simulating bursts of SSO assertions to ensure no transient admin actions succeed without a persisted membership state.
rollout_plan: Canary: Deploy change to canary runtime pool (dedicated infra zone) with feature-flag rbav2.defer_inflight_group_grants=true; route 2% of auth flows.
Monitor: Watch for false-positives (legitimate admin workflows blocked) via metrics: admin_action_block_rate, membership_reconcile_latency, failed_admin_ops_per_org.
Fallback: If customer impact increases, revert feature-flag and re-enable optimistic grants; escalate to on-call security lead.
Full rollout: After 72h stable canary and security review sign-off, flip flag cluster-wide and ship as rbac-2026.03 patch.
Audit fix: simultaneously deploy durable audit queue with 3x retry and dead-letter alerts; ensure audit consumer can backfill missing events from queue.
test_plan: Unit tests: precedence ordering, provisional-grant gating, and membership-write commit hooks.
Integration tests: end-to-end SSO group-sync simulation with nested groups and simultaneous service-token operations; verify no owner-level action allowed until membership persisted.
Load test: synthetic IdP burst (1k assertions/min) asserting durable audit queue retention and no dropped 'grant' events.
Security review: threat model updated, red-team scenario (intentional assertion replay) to ensure no bypass.
Customer regression harness: run against Org X's replication dataset (sanitized) before rolling to production.
